name: Joseph Smith as a child
voice: Boy about seven; light unforced mid pitch, rural New England coloring, intimate and brave without precocious wisdom. Cast a natural child performance or a suitable consenting adult performer; preserve breath and hesitation.
audition: Father, stay where I can see you. I think I can take another step.

name: Joseph Smith as a teenager
voice: Male fourteen to twenty; clear high baritone or tenor, plain northeastern American speech, earnest questions, occasional awkwardness. Gradual age progression rather than a digitally lowered child voice.
audition: They all speak with such certainty. I want to know what God would have me do.

name: Joseph Smith as a young adult
voice: Male early twenties to thirty; warm forward baritone, resonant but conversational, lively humor and a laborer's physical breath. Share identity and pronunciation with the mature Joseph voice.
states: affection; repentance; receiving revelation; leadership; exhaustion
audition: Oliver, read that sentence again. Let us be sure we have attended carefully.

name: Joseph Smith in his later ministry and celestial chapters
voice: Male thirty to thirty-eight in mortal scenes; broad warm baritone, vigorous public projection, musical dynamic phrasing, tender private register. Hopeful celestial Joseph retains his human warmth rather than becoming a processed bass deity. A reconstruction, since no authenticated sound recording survives.
states: consolation; conviction; sorrow; humor; fatigue; visionary joy
audition: Before I speak of the heavens, let me speak to the hearts that are grieving here.

name: Emma Hale Smith
voice: Female twenties to late thirties, warm clear mezzo with firm consonants, northeastern American coloring; practical intelligence, dignity and independent emotional presence. Speech and singing require separately approved takes.
states: affection; organization; disagreement; grief; prayer; restrained anger
audition: If this is to be a gathering, Joseph, then there must be a place for the people who arrive with nothing.

name: Oliver Cowdery
voice: Male early twenties to about thirty, clean articulate light baritone, a schoolteacher's precision, quick thought and quiet awe; distinguish from Joseph through a tighter rhythm rather than an affected accent.
audition: I have written it. Shall I read it back before we continue?

name: Hyrum Smith
voice: Male older than Joseph, grounded chest resonance, calm measured tempo, affectionate firmness. One recognizable identity ages gently from the family years into Carthage.
audition: You need not carry this hour alone. I am here with you.

name: Lucy Mack Smith
scope: Core 01 to 05 with later optional family scenes
voice: Female mature then older, warm low mezzo, New England cadences, direct maternal attention. Age through breath and texture without a caricatured tremor.
audition: Come inside, Joseph. You may tell me what troubles you when you are ready.

name: Joseph Smith Sr.
voice: Male mature, weathered low baritone, gentle rather than commanding, rural New England. A little physical effort in movement, no comic rustic voice.
audition: Take your time, son. I am listening.

name: Alvin Smith
voice: Male twenties, sturdy easy baritone, older-brother warmth, straightforward humor. The postmortal appearance preserves his identity.
audition: There will be time for the heavy work. Sit here with me a moment.

name: God the Father
voice: Male ageless mature presence, warm spacious low register with exceptional intelligibility and personal tenderness. Restraint and stillness carry authority. Distinct actor identity from Christ; no booming villain bass.
audition: This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!

name: Jesus Christ also identified as Jehovah
voice: Male adult, warm unforced baritone or low tenor, direct and merciful, clear close-microphone intimacy. Same voice identity across mortal recollection, revelation, and celestial scenes. Subtle spatial effects belong in mixing, not the training reference.
audition: There is room here for the one who has not yet been welcomed.

name: Moroni
voice: Male mature, clear luminous tenor-baritone, measured messenger cadence, concrete instruction with warmth. No wings or alien vocal processing implied by the voice.
audition: Receive this charge with care. What is entrusted to you is for the blessing of others.

name: John the Baptist
voice: Male mature, spare robust resonance, calm ceremonial clarity, slightly rougher texture than Moroni; respectful original English performance rather than an invented ancient accent.
audition: Attend to the responsibility that accompanies this authority.

name: Peter
voice: Male mature, firm clear baritone, direct leadership softened by kindness. Avoid treating an imagined biblical accent as authenticated.
audition: Serve together, and keep your hearts attentive to Christ.

name: James
voice: Male adult, focused middle register, concise steady delivery, clearly distinct from Peter and John.
audition: Let the work be carried in faithfulness.

name: John the Apostle
voice: Male adult, gentle clear tenor, reflective and precise, not frail or ethereal to the point of lost words.
audition: Let love remain in the work you are given.

name: Moses
voice: Male older, resonant and patient, sober phrasing without thunderous theatricality.
audition: Gather with a purpose that remembers every household.

name: Elias as named in Doctrine and Covenants 110
voice: Male adult, warm middle register, clear ceremonial diction. Distinguish from Elijah rather than resolving historical identity questions through voice casting.
audition: Let the promise be carried forward in faithful lives.

name: Elijah
voice: Male mature, deep but intimate resonance, a memorable gentle cadence around family and remembrance.
audition: Let the hearts of families turn toward one another.

name: Martin Harris
voice: Male forties, textured open baritone, rural New York speech, strong feeling and vulnerable sincerity. Financial sacrifice and distress are both audible.
audition: I have searched again. Joseph, I cannot find the pages.

name: David Whitmer
voice: Male twenties, balanced middle register, observant and deliberate, welcoming before becoming awed.
audition: The room is ready. You will have quiet enough to continue.

name: Peter Whitmer Sr.
voice: Male mature, hospitable low baritone, gentle German-American family influence only if supported by pronunciation research; keep intelligible and understated.
audition: Make a place at the table. There is room for another chair.

name: Isaac Hale
voice: Male mature, plain firm baritone, Pennsylvania rural coloring, protective father with reasons rather than a sneering antagonist.
audition: Emma's well-being matters to me. Tell me how you intend to provide for her.

name: Egbert B. Grandin
voice: Male twenties, businesslike bright baritone, brisk precise delivery, a printer discussing a real undertaking.
audition: Set the sheet where it can dry. The next impression must wait.

name: Newel Knight
voice: Male adult, open and sincere middle register, emotional without constant breathlessness.
audition: We have prepared what we can. The family is waiting inside.

name: Sidney Rigdon
voice: Male adult mature baritone, trained pulpit projection, elaborate phrase shapes, formidable public energy and a quieter reflective register. Avoid a permanently angry portrayal.
audition: A gathered people must learn what they owe one another.

name: Newel K. Whitney
voice: Male adult, grounded practical baritone, measured speech of a merchant and organizer.
audition: We can spare these provisions today. Tomorrow we shall need another plan.

name: Elizabeth Ann Whitney
voice: Female mature, warm low-middle register, composed decisive rhythm, both domestic hospitality and organizational authority.
audition: Ask what they need before deciding what we should bring.

name: Edward Partridge
voice: Male adult, steady thoughtful baritone, economical language, pressure heard as fatigue rather than aggression.
audition: I have counted the households. These are the families still without shelter.

name: John Johnson
voice: Male mature, low reassuring texture, plain household speech, quiet urgency.
audition: Bring clean water. We will stay with him until morning.

name: Brigham Young
voice: Male adult to older, compact plainspoken baritone, practical rhythms, strong resolve and flashes of private uncertainty. Older Salt Lake voice develops from the same identity.
audition: Then we begin with what is in front of us: the road, the families, and the work.

name: Heber C. Kimball
voice: Male adult, broad warm resonance, direct sturdy humor, quicker breath during travel.
audition: We can mend the wheel before dark if we work together.

name: Orson Pratt
voice: Male younger adult to older, precise curious light baritone, thoughtful pauses, mathematical clarity without a stereotypical eccentric scientist voice. Differentiate from Parley.
audition: When I consider the heavens, I find more questions to study, and more reasons to be humble.

name: Parley P. Pratt
voice: Male adult, expressive storyteller tenor-baritone, rhythmic warmth, distinctly more lyrical than Orson.
audition: Let me tell you how the message first reached our door.

name: Eliza R. Snow
voice: Female adult, composed lyrical mezzo, exact diction, poetic intelligence with practical authority. Never merely an ethereal chorus.
audition: I will keep the minutes. Let us make sure the work is remembered clearly.

name: Sarah M. Cleveland
voice: Female mature, brisk kind middle register, confident practical cadence.
audition: There is work enough for every willing hand, and care enough for every household.

name: William Clayton
voice: Male adult, restrained Lancashire English influence, exact careful diction, understated emotional responses. Research pronunciation before overemphasizing an accent.
audition: I have the wording here. Will you hear it once more before I make the copy?

name: Abraham Jonas
voice: Male mature, courteous assured middle-low register, civic and ceremonial delivery, British background handled subtly.
audition: Welcome, Mr. Smith. We will begin when the company is assembled.

name: Louisa Tanner Follett
voice: Female mature, grounded warm mezzo, grief expressed through effort and breath rather than perpetual sobbing. Her question should anchor the sermon.
audition: I can hear you speak of eternity. Help me know how to face the morning.

name: Willard Richards
voice: Male mature, calm low baritone, British coloring, precise observation; composure does not remove feeling.
audition: I am here. Tell me what you need me to write.

name: Wilford Woodruff
voice: Male adult, clear attentive middle register, Connecticut coloring, quiet urgency as a recorder.
audition: I will set down what I can while it is fresh in my mind.

name: Thomas Bullock
voice: Male adult, precise Staffordshire English influence, brisk focused light baritone; distinguish from Clayton through pacing.
audition: The crowd was still when he turned to the family.

name: John Taylor
voice: Male adult, warm resonant English baritone; capable of an unforced hymn performance. Prepare spoken and sung voice references separately and retain the same identity.
audition: Would you like me to sing it again?

name: Dan Jones
voice: Male adult, Welsh-influenced clear tenor-baritone, lively warmth and restrained concern.
audition: I will take your message. Is there anything else you wish me to carry?

name: Martin Van Buren
voice: Male older adult, formal measured northeastern American delivery; political reserve rather than theatrical cruelty.
audition: I understand the seriousness of the petition you have brought.

name: Governor Thomas Ford
voice: Male mature, formal legal diction, controlled middle-low register, ambiguous confidence and public responsibility.
audition: Your case will be heard through the legal process.

name: William Law
voice: Male mature, firm articulate baritone, principled opposition and real disappointment; no hiss, sneer, or secret-villain affect.
audition: I believe these questions must be answered openly.

name: Composite Methodist minister
voice: Male adult, open energetic tenor, earnest revival cadence and warmth; sincere period belief rather than villainous manipulation.
audition: Bring your questions, young man. We ought to speak earnestly about the soul.

name: Composite Presbyterian minister
voice: Male mature, measured low baritone, structured scriptural argument, patient seriousness.
audition: Let us begin with the scripture you have been considering.

name: Composite Baptist minister
voice: Male adult, clear firm middle register, practical questions and sincere conviction.
audition: Tell me what you understand by faith, and we can speak of baptism.

name: Composite townspeople voice family
voice: Two distinct adult voices, one female alto and one male tenor, plain local speech. Maintain named preset suffixes for each actor so one identity does not accidentally change mid-conversation.
audition: The road is passable beyond the bridge. You may wait here until the rain eases.

name: Composite refugee voice family
voice: Two adults with distinct restrained registers; fatigue and dignity, no generic suffering accent. The historical journal identifies composite testimony.
audition: We brought the children through. Now we need a dry place for the night.

name: Composite officers and guard voice family
voice: Two male adult registers, clipped practical authority; variations include courteous, uncertain, and hostile, without conflating different historical offices.
audition: You will need to come with us. Bring the papers you wish to present.

name: Composite Kirtland depositor
voice: Female adult, clear low-middle register, controlled fear about a household's losses; neither foolish nor malicious.
audition: These notes were our savings. I need to know how we will buy food.

name: Composite Smith household child
voice: Natural school-age child, curious and ordinary, light clear register with varied pacing. Do not use a baby voice or a digitally pitch-shifted Joseph.
audition: Will you have time to walk with us when you come home?

name: Composite mourner
voice: Female mature, plain direct alto, honest grief and thoughtful attention. Keep any postmortal reuse a clearly fictional person rather than implying Louisa dies in 1844.
audition: I believe there is hope. Today I need help holding on to it.

name: Composite mob voices
voice: Small ensemble of distinct male adults; brief urgent distant shouts, no relish or cartoon evil. Keep violence subordinate to the victims' experience.
audition: They are upstairs!

name: Miriam a fictional celestial mission guide
voice: Female adult, warm clear mezzo, lucid technical language, patience and gentle humor. An ordinary human identity after transformation; no synthetic oracle effect.
audition: We have learned to cross the years. We are still learning how to care for the people within them.

name: Elias Vale a fictional Zion scientist
voice: Male adult, inquisitive light baritone, calm contemporary clarity, humane and fallible. This character is not the Elias of Doctrine and Covenants 110.
audition: We can open the crossing. We cannot decide another person's life for them.

name: Ruth a fictional 1955 missionary
voice: Female young adult, clear mid-century American diction, enthusiastic but reflective, no parody of vintage radio.
audition: We came to offer help. You are free to tell us what would actually be useful.

name: Daniel a fictional 1994 family archivist
voice: Male adult, ordinary warm tenor, understated humor and deep attachment to remembered people.
audition: There is another tape in the drawer. I thought no one would ever ask about it.

name: Ada a fictional present-day caretaker
voice: Female adult, confident low-middle register, technical competence with a quiet contemplative pace.
audition: If the garden is to survive the summer, we have to share the water fairly.

name: Mara a fictional future desert survivor
voice: Female mature, dry tired alto, practical skepticism and resilient warmth. Illness never becomes a monster vocal effect.
audition: Do not promise me a paradise. Help me keep this well running until morning.

name: The fictional custodian of the closed archive
voice: Male mature, polished restrained baritone, persuasive sincere claims about order; an understandable antagonist who can reconsider.
audition: If everyone chooses freely, we may lose the future we have guarded.
